record.paper_title: The solution of Hutník’s open problem
record.original_question: Let (X,A) be a measurable space, let F_(X,A) be the class of all A-measurable functions f:X->[0,1], and let M_(X,A) be the class of capacities mu:A->[0,1], meaning nondecreasing set functions with mu(empty set)=0 and mu(X)=1. A semicopula S:[0,1]^2->[0,1] is a binary operation that is nondecreasing in each coordinate and has neutral element 1. For such a semicopula define the smallest semicopula-based integral I_S(mu,f)=sup over t in [0,1] of S(t, mu({x in X: f(x)>=t})). Which semicopulas S have the translation-invariance property I_S(mu,f+a)=I_S(mu,f)+a for every measurable space (X,A), every capacity mu in M_(X,A), every measurable f in F_(X,A), and every a in [0,1] such that f+a is still [0,1]-valued?

evidence.quote: Characterize a class of semicopulas S, for which the equality I_S(mu,f+a)=I_S(mu,f)+a holds for each (X,A), each (mu,f) and a.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{A})$ be a measurable space. Denote by $\mathcal{F}_{(X,\mathcal{A})}$ the class of all $\mathcal{A}$-measurable functions $f:X\to[0,1]$, and by $\mathcal{M}_{(X,\mathcal{A})}$ the class of capacities $\mu:\mathcal{A}\to[0,1]$, i.e., set functions that are nondecreasing, satisfy $\mu(\emptyset)=0$ and $\mu(X)=1$. A semicopula is a function $S:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ that is nondecreasing in each coordinate and has $1$ as a neutral element (i.e., $S(1,x)=S(x,1)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$). For a semicopula $S$, define the smallest semicopula-based integral
$$ I_S(\mu,f) \;=\; \sup_{t\in[0,1]} S\bigl(t,\;\mu(\{x\in X:f(x)\ge t\})\bigr). $$
Characterize all semicopulas $S$ for which the translation-invariance property
$$ I_S(\mu,f+a) \;=\; I_S(\mu,f)+a $$
holds for every measurable space $(X,\mathcal{A})$, every capacity $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_{(X,\mathcal{A})}$, every $f\in\mathcal{F}_{(X,\mathcal{A})}$, and every $a\in[0,1]$ such that $f+a$ still takes values in $[0,1]$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (posed by Hutník) has been solved: the only semicopula for which the smallest semicopula-based integral is translation invariant in the stated sense is the Łukasiewicz t-norm $S(x,y)=\max(x+y-1,0)$. This characterization is established in the zbMATH-indexed work titled "The solution of Hutník's open problem."

status_evidence.title: The solution of Hutník's open problem (zbMATH)
status_evidence.snippet: Characterize a class of semicopulas S, for which the equality I_S(mu,f+a)=I_S(mu,f)+a holds ... contains only the Łukasiewicz t-norm.
status_evidence.claim: The class of semicopulas with the translation invariance property consists solely of the Łukasiewicz t-norm.

status_evidence.title: Semicopula based integrals - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Semicopula-based integrals generalize Sugeno and Shilkret integrals; bounds by the Łukasiewicz t-norm play a special role.
status_evidence.claim: The Łukasiewicz t-norm plays a distinguished role among semicopulas in semicopula-based integration theory.
